dedupe_keys.name: the lockdown effect implications of the covid 19 pandemic on internet traffic feldmann et al 2020

description: This measurement study examines how COVID-19 lockdowns changed Internet traffic, using data from one ISP, three IXPs and one metropolitan educational network. Confinement raised residential demand for remote working, entertainment, commerce and education and shifted traffic in the Internet core. Traffic volume grew 15 to 20 percent almost within a week, a modest but fast rise, and the infrastructure handled it because most shifts occurred outside traditional peak hours. Hypergiants still contributed a large share, but non-hypergiants grew faster, applications used at home such as web conferencing, VPN and gaming increased, and academic networks saw large overall decreases with rises in remote working and lecturing applications. Producer: a twelve-author team, versions submitted 25 August 2020 and revised 5 October 2020. Coverage: vantage points in Europe (one ISP, three IXPs, one educational network, locations not read). Access: free arXiv preprint; only the abstract was read, and the underlying traffic data are not released on the page. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: an arXiv e-print not peer-reviewed by arXiv, based on the vantage points named. Simulation uses: the demand growth and daily shift provide scenario parameters for capacity-planning and resilience models of exchange and access networks. Related records: the Iberian blackout IXP case study (case_study-iberian-blackout-2025-internet-exchange-points-traffic-bgp-data-centre) and Euro-IX IXP reports (data-euro-ix-ixp-reports).
